Jamie — a couple of pragmatic framing points from pricing:

1) Commitment bands: our standard commercial anchors are 6% uplift for 12-month prepay on retention (vs. paygo), but for larger ARR we can layer up front credits that effectively increase discount to the numbers Kim called out (10/18/28). We’ll need a signed MSA + SOW to lock the deeper tiers.
2) Archival taper: we treat taper as a schedule of unit-rate multipliers by age band. The PDF has three examples; the one I recommend for heavy archival customers is the conservative taper (60/30/10) because it keeps egress and restore economics aligned.
3) Seatless tracing: we can model either (a) strict per-10k traces tiers, or (b) percentile-based billing (p90 traces/day) — the latter is preferred for bursty telemetry. For pilot credits, we typically provide 30–90 day credits tied to an onboarding milestone.

Pricing ask: if AcroHealth is comfortable sharing an approximate monthly trace volume and retention split (hot: <90d, warm: 90–365d, cold: >365d), I’ll produce a clean quote and a simple sample invoice row for procurement.

Arjun — thanks for the numbers, that’s very helpful. A few technical clarifications that affect cost:

- Trace normalization: if traces are aggregated/normalized at ingest we can reduce billable units ~20–30% depending on retention policy. If you enable prefix/kv caching we can compress request counts further.
- Cold restores: we support a staged restore (tiered egress) that keeps cold restores at a lower per-GB rate, but there’s a per-restore minimum. The archival taper numbers in the PDF assume a 1% monthly restore profile; if you cap restores at 5% we’ll need to adjust the cold band multiplier up by ~1.8x.
- Dashboards: we can offer an org-wide entitlement (single invoice line) with an adoption-based uplift after 6 months (if license seats exceed three projects we step up the fee).

I’ll take these inputs and update the workbook with a p90 billing projection for tracing, two normalization scenarios, and an adjusted archival taper for the 5% restore cap.
